desk.headline: Sales up 6% to DKK 79.2bn and adjusted operating profit up 34%, beat; 2026 outlook raised for a third time
results: Sales rose 6% to DKK 79.2bn (4% at constant currency), with both US (+2%) and International (+10%) growing.
Obesity care sales grew 24% to DKK 26.1bn, led by the new Wegovy pill at DKK 5.4bn; Wegovy injections were flat and Ozempic fell 3%.
Adjusted operating profit jumped 34% to DKK 31.7bn, partly because last year's quarter carried DKK 9bn of restructuring costs.
Reported profit fell: DKK 8.7bn of impairments (ziltivekimab and a smaller factory network) cut diluted EPS to DKK 3.79 from DKK 4.50.
Nine-month free cash flow reached DKK 83.8bn; DKK 10.0bn of shares were bought back in the period.

guidance.summary: Novo raised its 2026 outlook for adjusted sales and adjusted operating profit to between a 2% fall and a 2% rise at constant currency, from a 0-6% fall, and lifted its free cash flow target. It also cut US list prices for Wegovy and Ozempic from January, which it expects to weigh on 2027 cash flow.

points: CEO Mike Doustdar stressed that both US and International sales grew, and that growth was led by obesity drugs.
He said lower prices are driving volume: "we made our products more affordable."
The Wegovy pill has passed 8 million US prescriptions since its January launch, and should reach more than 20 markets in 2027.
From 1 January the US list prices of Wegovy and Ozempic fall by about 50% and 35%.
Novo is preparing a US launch of CagriSema in early 2027, subject to approval.
